findings.claim: The errata ledger is not printed in the book. A reader holding only the PDF sees each correction in place but has no single table of what changed from the first edition, which is the document a teacher comparing the two editions needs.
findings.evidence: build/Biopharmaceutics_and_Pharmacokinetics_PT312.md contains no 'Errata Ledger' heading; harness/tools/assemble.py emits front matter, chapters and the configured back matter only, and the spec's INV-41 lists front_matter, chapter_glob and glossary. The front matter no longer promises it at the back, so the book is self-consistent, but the ledger reaches the reader only with the course materials.
findings.fix_hint: Add an opt-in template flag for printing the errata file as back matter, defaulting off so no existing book changes, then set it for this project.

findings.claim: The corrected text has not been read by an independent reviewer. The one Codex review permitted per artifact under Rule 11 was spent on the pre-fix build, and the twenty fixes it prompted were written and verified by the same agent that wrote the chapters.
findings.evidence: audit/codex-audit.md records reviewed_commit b6a32b5; the fixes land in 1472d00. Every fix was confirmed against the text and, where numeric, recomputed independently before being applied, but no second party has read the result.
findings.fix_hint: If a second review is wanted, run it against the current build as a separate artifact and record it beside this one.

findings.claim: Four worked examples use illustrative constants rather than data from the source notes, so a student cannot trace them back to the lectures.
findings.evidence: ch11 Example 11.1, ch13 Example 13.1 and ch14 Example 14.1 each open by saying the constants are illustrative. The source's own datasets were exhausted by the other eleven examples; these three topics carried no numeric example in the first edition.
findings.fix_hint: Leave as is, or replace with figures from a named published study so the provenance is citable.

findings.claim: Citation numbers are chapter-local, so [2] means different works in different chapters, and the consolidated list at the back carries a third numbering of its own.
findings.evidence: check_book.check_citations resolves every [n] against the reference list in the same file, so per-chapter lists cannot be removed. references.md therefore repeats the eight works under its own numbering, with the citing chapters named in each entry.
findings.fix_hint: Number the consolidated list once and have chapters cite those numbers, which needs the citation checker to resolve against a book-level list.

findings.claim: Eight works support fourteen chapters, and two textbooks carry most of it: Shargel is cited in all fourteen chapters and Rowland in twelve.
findings.evidence: Counted from the per-chapter reference lists. The regulatory and compendial chapters are better sourced: ICH M9, ICH M13A, the EDA guideline v4/2026, USP <711>, USP <724> and Amidon 1995 are each cited where they apply.
findings.fix_hint: Add primary sources for the physiological and metabolic chapters, which currently rest on the two textbooks alone.
